title: OBJ and STL
sub: Simple, old and understood by everyone
cards/0/title: OBJ: a text file from the 80s
cards/0/body:
Wavefront created OBJ in the late 1980s. It is plain text: a v line is a vertex, vt is a UV, vn is a normal, f is a face made of vertex numbers (counting from one). Materials live in a separate .mtl file.

It opens in Notepad and in almost any 3D program.
cards/0/deep: f 1/1/1 means the position, UV and normal numbers. A face can be a quad or an n-gon: OBJ does not require triangles. Negative indices count from the end. There is no hierarchy or animation: o and g are just group names.
cards/1/body:
STL was created in 1987 for stereolithography (by 3D Systems). Inside there are only triangles: each has a normal and three vertices. No color, no UVs, no units.

It comes in text and binary flavors. Binary: an 80-byte header, the triangle count, and 50 bytes per triangle.
cards/2/task: Build the house from front-facing triangles and compare how many bytes and vertices go into OBJ and into STL.
cards/3/q: Complete the OBJ face from vertices 1, 2, 3
cards/3/explain: f stands for face. The numbers refer to the v lines in order, starting from one.
cards/4/q: How big is a binary STL with 1,000 triangles?
cards/4/explain: 84 bytes of header and counter + 1,000 × 50 bytes: normal 12, three vertices 36, attribute bytes 2.
cards/5/q: Why is STL still the standard in 3D printing?
cards/5/options/0: A printer only needs the shape, and STL is the simplest, most widely understood way to send it
cards/5/explain: A slicer needs a closed volume made of triangles. STL does not need anything else.
cards/5/deep: There is also the newer 3MF for printing: units, colors, materials and multiple objects in one zip file. Slicer support for it keeps growing.
cards/6/q: Which line of the text STL holds the normal?
cards/6/explain: facet normal is the triangle’s normal, followed by three vertex lines.
cards/7/q: What gets lost if you save a game character as STL? Select all.
cards/7/explain: Only the shape, made of triangles, survives.
